findings.title: Security Release 0.4.9.15
findings.summary_md: Tor 0.4.9.15 was released with several security fixes, among them three new denial-of-service defenses intended to handle the thunderstorm of directory requests the network was seeing. Tor developer David Goulet pointed relay and bridge operators to a tor-relays mailing list email for details of the new defenses and asked them to upgrade as soon as possible. Debian packages were published with the release. This is the first build in the series that leads to 0.4.9.17.

findings.title: Security Release 0.4.9.16
findings.summary_md: Tor 0.4.9.16 was an emergency release containing only a handful of fixes for directory authorities. The announcement described a thundering herd situation in which a large number of outdated clients stuck in restart loops repeatedly fetched directory information, loading the few relays serving as fallback directories and the directory authorities themselves. Until a better long-term solution exists, the authorities temporarily allowed those older clients to rejoin the network to stabilize load. Upgrading was recommended but described as not urgent unless the operator runs a directory authority.

findings.title: Security Release 0.4.9.17
findings.summary_md: Tor 0.4.9.17 includes a series of security fixes, one of which Goulet called especially important for relay DoS defenses because of how they deal with IPv6 handling. The release came as a rapid response to the ongoing DDoS attack that had affected most relay operators, with relays overwhelmed by a massive flood of client circuits. The project said it was actively evaluating additional defenses and expected further releases in the near future, and asked operators to upgrade as soon as possible with no action item required afterwards.

findings.title: Security Release 0.4.9.14
findings.summary_md: Tor 0.4.9.14 addressed a series of high-severity security issues affecting clients, onion services, directory authorities and relays, with detailed ticket information withheld for at least another week per project policy. The announcement stated the project was on a rapid release cadence and that the next release would more likely arrive in the last week of October or first week of November. That forecast matches the 0.4.9.15 release on 28 October that introduced the new directory-request DoS defenses.
